title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a Grothendieck manuscript. It is a typed page of a Bourbaki draft ('rédaction' n° 392, page 6-25). It is the exercise set for Commutative Algebra ch. VII ('Diviseurs'), §3 on factorial rings, and was evidently misfiled among Grothendieck's handwritten L-function notes. The neighbouring pages, on inertia invariants E^I, the maps R(D|U,k) → R(D|I,k) and L-series, are unrelated.

Exercise 6 c), d): rings of the form k[X,Y]/(aX²+bY²+1).
- Over an ordered field with a, b > 0, the conic has no rational points. One shows the coordinate ring is a UFD using the previous part and a criterion from §1, ex. 17.
- d) C = ℚ[X,Y]/(X²+2Y²+1) is factorial. After base change to ℚ(i), the relation X²+1 = (X+i)(X−i) = −2Y² gives a non-unique factorization, so C⊗ℚ(i) is not factorial. This is the classical example that factoriality does not descend-and-ascend under field extension.

Exercise 7: Samuel's theorem on cyclic covers of weighted-homogeneous hypersurfaces.
- Setting: K is a noetherian UFD and F ∈ K[X_1..X_n] is prime and quasi-homogeneous of weight q. Adjoin z with z^c = F, where gcd(c,q) = 1.
- Claim: A = K[X, z] is factorial if (1) c ≡ 1 mod q, or (2) finitely generated projective K-modules are free.
- Hint for (1): A[1/z] is factorial; then use Nagata's criterion (prop. 3).
- Hint for (2): pass to B = A[z'] with z'^d = z and cd ≡ 1 mod q. Grade with z' of weight q and X_i of weight cdq(i), so that z'^{cd} = F is homogeneous. Reduce to showing Au ∩ Av is principal for homogeneous u, v, using B free over A.
- Corollary: K[X,Y,Z]/(Z^a − X^b − Y^c) is factorial when a, b, c are pairwise coprime (Brieskorn–Samuel type examples).

Exercise 8 (beginning): setup for Samuel's counterexample showing that A factorial does not imply A[[T]] factorial.
- Data: x extremal (prime) with Ax ∩ Ay = Axy, and integers i, j, k with ijk − ij − jk − ki ≥ 0 (e.g. (2,3,7)) and z^i ∈ Ax^j + Ay^k.
- One constructs v = xy − z^{i−1}T and a series v' over B = A[1/x] with vv' ∈ A[[T]]. This exhibits a non-principal divisorial ideal in A[[T]].
errors: No mathematical errors detected. The weight bookkeeping in the hint to ex. 7 is consistent: z'^{cd} = F has weight cdq on both sides.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a misfiled typed Bourbaki draft page of standard, published exercises due to Samuel. Nothing here is Grothendieck's own or absent from the literature. The only point of archival interest is the misfiling.
transcription_corrections: 'Q' should be read as ℚ (rationals) in exercise 6 d).
The page header '6 - 25 - n° 392' is a Bourbaki rédaction number, not part of the L-function notes; the handwritten '41' at bottom left is the archive folio.
